item.title: Review: In New Zealand’s bellwether seat, what are locals thinking as a knife-edge poll looms?
item.description: When the Guardian visited the Maungakiekie electorate, two themes emerge: a grudging fealty to the National party and growing support for minor parties It’s a hot spring day in the Auckland suburb of Onehunga, and the main strip is starting to hum with life. Builders slip into a bakery for a snack, retirees chat over coffee outside cafes and a shoeless man zips by on a scooter. There are few signs New Zealand’s general election is looming along this shopping strip but Onehunga and neighbouring suburbs that make up the electorate Maungakiekie, will be closely watched when New Zealand heads to the polls on 7 November. item.title: Review: Cosplay any day: the growing community bringing costumes to the streets
item.description: No longer confined to conventions, an increasing number of Australian cosplayers are gathering for casual meet-ups, and making friends along the way Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email Willow* and her friends know they are always the first to be spotted in a crowd. They don’t mind the stares. Sitting at the steps of Sydney’s town hall, the trio are an island of pastel pink, lavender and fiery red, the intensity of their wigs matched by the extravagance of their makeup. Willow’s face is artfully made up, her eyes embellished with bright blue eyeshadow, thick winged eyeliner and spiky false lashes. A pair of platform Converse lifts her an extra 5cm above ground. Sign up for the fun…
